name.zh: 育空 1 号公路——阿拉斯加公路

tagline.en: Built in nine months as an act of war, and still measured in the mileposts of 1942
tagline.zh: 作为战时工程在九个月内建成，至今仍沿用 1942 年的里程桩

start.en: The British Columbia boundary south of Watson Lake, at historic kilometre 968
start.zh: 沃森湖以南的不列颠哥伦比亚省界，历史桩号 968 公里处

end.en: The Alaska border east of Beaver Creek, at historic kilometre 1,874, where the road continues as Alaska Route 2
end.zh: 比弗克里克以东的阿拉斯加州界，历史桩号 1,874 公里处，其后接阿拉斯加 2 号公路

en: The Alaska Highway is the reason there is a road network in the Yukon at all. It runs 906 kilometres across the territory on the historic chainage, from the British Columbia boundary through Watson Lake and Whitehorse to the Alaska border, and every other Yukon highway hangs off it.

It is also a reminder of what a northern road is. Of the Yukon's 4,830 kilometres of road, only about 350 kilometres — seven per cent — carry conventional pavement. Roughly 2,500 kilometres are gravel, and most of the rest is bituminous surface treatment, a sprayed-and-chipped surface that behaves like pavement in summer and like something else in the spring thaw.

Traffic is correspondingly thin. A consultant's report for the Skagway port put the Alaska Highway at around 500 vehicles a day in 2005, rising to about 800 in summer. Distances from Whitehorse give the scale better than any traffic figure does: Dawson Creek, where the highway starts, is 1,426 kilometres away; Fairbanks is 951; Inuvik is 1,222.
zh: 育空之所以存在公路网，全赖阿拉斯加公路。按历史桩号计，它在育空境内长 906 公里，自不列颠哥伦比亚省界经沃森湖、白马市直抵阿拉斯加州界；育空其余各条公路，无一不是从它身上分出去的。
它同时也提醒着人们，北方的路是什么样子。育空全境 4,830 公里道路中，只有约 350 公里——百分之七——铺设了常规路面。约 2,500 公里是砾石路，余下大部分为沥青表面处治：一种喷洒沥青再撒布碎石的路面，夏天像铺装路，春季融冻期就是另一回事了。
车流量与之相称地稀少。一份为斯卡圭港所作的顾问报告称，2005 年阿拉斯加公路日均约 500 辆车，夏季升至约 800 辆。比任何流量数字更能说明尺度的，是自白马市出发的里程：公路起点道森克里克远在 1,426 公里之外，费尔班克斯 951 公里，伊努维克 1,222 公里。

en: Japan attacked Pearl Harbor in December 1941. Roosevelt approved an overland route to Alaska on 11 February 1942, Canada and the United States settled the construction agreement on 18 March, and work began that month. Canada supplied the right-of-way and waived customs duties; the United States built the road and agreed to maintain it for the duration of the war.

Around 11,000 soldiers and some 16,000 Canadian and American civilians cut a pioneer road of more than 1,500 miles through muskeg and permafrost, with 133 bridges of six metres or longer. The last gap closed near Beaver Creek on 25 October 1942, and the highway was opened to military traffic at Soldiers Summit above Kluane Lake on 20 November — under ten months from the first survey. Many of the troops who built it were Black soldiers drafted after the Selective Service Act of 1940, assigned to segregated regiments in one of the coldest construction environments on the continent.

The permanent all-weather road followed in 1943, and by the end of that year Dawson Creek and Fairbanks were linked. Canada took over the Canadian portion on 1 April 1946, repaying the United States for its construction in order to extinguish any future American claim to the road. It opened to the general public in 1948, and was designated a National Historic Event in 1954. Parks Canada's own plaque does not describe this as an unmixed good: the highway, it says, "opened the Northwest to southern exploitation of natural resources, altering Yukon settlement patterns and changing Native ways of life".
zh: 1941 年 12 月，日本袭击珍珠港。1942 年 2 月 11 日，罗斯福批准修建一条通往阿拉斯加的陆路；3 月 18 日，美加议定施工协议，当月开工。加拿大提供路权并免征关税；美国负责修路，并承诺在战争期间维护。

约 11,000 名军人与约 16,000 名加美两国平民，在泥沼与永久冻土中开出一条一千五百余英里的先导路，架起 133 座六米以上的桥梁。1942 年 10 月 25 日，最后一处缺口在比弗克里克附近合龙；11 月 20 日，公路在克卢恩湖畔的「士兵岭」向军事运输开放——距首次勘测不足十个月。参与修筑的士兵中有许多是《1940 年选征兵役法》后应征入伍的黑人军人，他们被编入种族隔离建制的团队，投入北美最寒冷的施工环境之一。

1943 年建成全天候永久路面，当年年底道森克里克与费尔班克斯全线贯通。1946 年 4 月 1 日，加拿大接管境内路段，并向美国偿付其施工费用，以消除美方日后对这条路可能提出的任何权利主张。1948 年向公众开放，1954 年被定为国家历史事件。加拿大公园管理局自己的纪念牌并未将此描述为纯粹的好事：牌文称，这条公路「使西北地区门户洞开，任由南方开发其自然资源，改变了育空的聚落格局，也改变了原住民的生活方式」。

en: The kilometre posts along the highway are not the distance you have driven. They are the 1942 chainage, and sixty years of realignment shortened the road without renumbering the posts. The federal government still describes the British Columbia–Yukon boundary as kilometre 968 while British Columbia's own measured inventory puts it about 954.5 kilometres from Dawson Creek — roughly thirteen and a half kilometres of highway that history has quietly removed. Neither figure is wrong; they are answering different questions.

One road, three landlords. British Columbia took over the first 133 kilometres in 1961. The next 835 kilometres, to the Yukon boundary, remain federal property, maintained by Public Services and Procurement Canada — an unusual arrangement in which Ottawa directly operates a highway. The Yukon assumed its 906 kilometres on 1 April 1992.
The name is younger than the road. It was the Alcan Highway until Canada and the United States exchanged diplomatic notes on 19 July 1943 settling on Alaska Highway.
zh: 沿途的公里桩并不是你已经驶过的距离。它们是 1942 年的桩号，而六十年的线路改造缩短了道路，桩号却未重编。联邦政府至今仍把不列颠哥伦比亚与育空的省界记作 968 公里桩，而不列颠哥伦比亚自己的实测台账显示该处距道森克里克约 954.5 公里——约十三点五公里的公路，被历史悄悄抹去了。两个数字都不算错，它们回答的是不同的问题。
一条路，三个业主。1961 年，不列颠哥伦比亚接管了起始的 133 公里。此后至育空省界的 835 公里仍属联邦财产，由加拿大公共服务和采购部维护——渥太华直接运营一条公路，这种安排颇为罕见。育空则于 1992 年 4 月 1 日接管其境内的 906 公里。
路名比路年轻。在 1943 年 7 月 19 日美加互换外交换文定名「阿拉斯加公路」之前，它一直叫「阿尔坎公路」。

value.en: 906 km, from historic kilometre 968 at the British Columbia boundary to kilometre 1,874 at the Alaska border. A widely repeated alternative is 957.15 km; the 51 km difference is consistent with posted chainage against measured distance, and the two could not be reconciled.
value.zh: 906 公里，自省界处的历史桩号 968 公里至阿拉斯加州界处的 1,874 公里。另一广为流传的数字是 957.15 公里；51 公里的差距与「桩号里程对实测里程」的差异相符，两者无法对齐。

figures.source: Public Services and Procurement Canada, About the Alaska Highway; alternative figure per published route lists

value.en: About 2,450 km from Dawson Creek, British Columbia to Delta Junction, Alaska, of which roughly 1,900 km — about 80 per cent — is in Canada
value.zh: 自不列颠哥伦比亚省道森克里克至阿拉斯加州三角洲枢纽约 2,450 公里，其中约 1,900 公里（约 80%）在加拿大境内

figures.source: Public Services and Procurement Canada, About the Alaska Highway

value.en: US$130.6 million for the original military road of more than 1,500 miles, built in under nine months. The Canadian Encyclopedia gives about $185 million to complete; the two figures conflict and the scope of the second is not stated.
value.zh: 最初的军用道路造价 1.306 亿美元，全长一千五百余英里，工期不足九个月。《加拿大百科全书》给出的完工造价约为 1.85 亿元；两个数字互相矛盾，且后者未说明其统计范围。

figures.source: FHWA, Contributions and Crossroads: Alaska Highway Fact Sheet; The Canadian Encyclopedia

value.en: The Yukon budgeted $11.846 million for the Alaska Highway in 2025–26, out of $49.416 million for all territorial highways — the largest single line in the territory's road budget.
value.zh: 2025–26 年度，育空为阿拉斯加公路编列预算 1,184.6 万元，全境公路预算合计 4,941.6 万元——这是该地区道路预算中最大的单项。

figures.source: Government of Yukon, Highways and Public Works 2025-26 Supplementary Information, Expenditures by Highway

value.en: Across the Yukon network, about 350 km is conventional pavement, 1,880 km bituminous surface treatment and roughly 1,500 km gravel on primary highways alone. There is no date on which the Alaska Highway was fully paved, because in the conventional sense it never was.
value.zh: 在育空全境路网中，仅干线公路就有约 350 公里常规铺装、1,880 公里沥青表面处治、约 1,500 公里砾石路面。阿拉斯加公路并不存在「全线铺装完成」的日期，因为在常规意义上它从未被全线铺装。

figures.source: Government of Yukon, Highways and Public Works 2025-26 Supplementary Information

value.en: About 500 vehicles a day in 2005, rising to roughly 800 a day in summer. Yukon publishes station-level counts in its Traffic Count Summary, but the most recent edition traced is 2011 and its tables could not be retrieved.
value.zh: 2005 年日均约 500 辆，夏季升至约 800 辆。育空在《交通量统计汇编》中公布逐站观测数据，但可查到的最新版本为 2011 年，且未能取得其数据表。

figures.source: Skagway Port Development Plan, section 2 (consultant report; underlying territorial counts not obtained)

value.en: No published figure for the Yukon section. On the British Columbia portion the summit is Summit Pass, 1,267 m, about 140 km north of Fort Nelson.
value.zh: 育空段无公开数据。不列颠哥伦比亚段的最高点为峰顶山口，海拔 1,267 米，位于纳尔逊堡以北约 140 公里。

figures.source: British Columbia Ministry of Transportation and Infrastructure, highway elevations table

timeline.en: Roosevelt approves the route on 11 February and construction begins in March. The pioneer road's last gap closes near Beaver Creek on 25 October, and the highway opens to military traffic at Soldiers Summit on 20 November.
timeline.zh: 2 月 11 日罗斯福批准该线路，3 月开工。10 月 25 日先导路最后一处缺口在比弗克里克附近合龙，11 月 20 日于士兵岭向军事运输开放。

timeline.en: The permanent all-weather road is built, linking Dawson Creek and Fairbanks by year's end. Canada and the United States settle on the name Alaska Highway on 19 July.
timeline.zh: 建成全天候永久道路，年底前贯通道森克里克与费尔班克斯。7 月 19 日，美加两国定名「阿拉斯加公路」。

timeline.en: Canada takes over the Canadian portion on 1 April, repaying the United States its construction cost.
timeline.zh: 4 月 1 日加拿大接管境内路段，并向美国偿付施工费用。

timeline.en: The highway opens to the general public.
The Alaska Highway is designated a National Historic Event on 7 June.
timeline.zh: 6 月 7 日，阿拉斯加公路被定为国家历史事件。

timeline.en: British Columbia assumes the first 133 km, from Dawson Creek to north of Fort St John.
timeline.zh: 不列颠哥伦比亚接管起始 133 公里，自道森克里克至圣约翰堡以北。

timeline.en: Operations of the 835 km federal section pass to the department that is today Public Services and Procurement Canada.
timeline.zh: 联邦管辖的 835 公里路段移交给今日的加拿大公共服务和采购部运营。

timeline.en: The Yukon assumes responsibility for its 906 km on 1 April.
timeline.zh: 4 月 1 日，育空接管境内 906 公里。
